ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows an organic structure; in the upper left is a nitrogen labeled HN, the nitrogen is connected to a short line indicating a methyl substituent, and is connected to the central carbon below; the right side of the central carbon is connected to OH, the lower left continues to connect to a segment of carbon chain, and the terminal is labeled CHO. There are also curved arrows and small arrows in the figure, but the question requires ignoring these arrows. Then reason: After ignoring the arrows, the skeleton connection relationship is CH3-NH-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-CHO. Written according to linear SMILES, methyl connected to nitrogen is CN, nitrogen connected to the carbon containing hydroxyl is CNC(O), then connected to two methylenes and ending with an aldehyde group, giving CNC(O)CCC=O.

method.method_draft: First inspect the molecule in the image and disregard all arrow markings as instructed. Identify the connectivity as CH3-NH-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-CHO: the methyl-substituted amine is attached to the alcohol-bearing carbon, which is connected to a propanal tail. Then encode this connectivity linearly in SMILES as CNC(O)CCC=O.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中显示一个有机结构，左上方是标注为 HN 的氮，氮上连有一个短线表示甲基取代基，并与下方的中心碳相连；中心碳右侧连有 OH，左下方继续连接一段碳链，末端标注为 CHO。图中还有弯曲箭头和小箭头，但题目要求忽略这些箭头。
再推理：忽略箭头后，骨架连接关系为 CH3-NH-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-CHO。按线性 SMILES 书写，甲基接氮为 CN，氮接含羟基的碳为 CNC(O)，再接两个亚甲基并以醛基结尾，得到 CNC(O)CCC=O。

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the displayed skeletal structure while ignoring the curved arrows: an N bearing one H and a methyl substituent is bonded to a central carbon; that central carbon also bears an OH group and continues through a three-carbon chain ending in an aldehyde group labeled CHO.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to determine the task: select/write the SMILES expression for the transition-state structure and ignore the arrows.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use organic skeletal-structure conventions: line ends/vertices are carbons with implicit hydrogens; labeled HN with a methyl substituent gives CH3NH-; OH is attached to the central carbon; terminal CHO is an aldehyde and can be written as C=O in SMILES when the aldehydic H is implicit. Convert the connected atom sequence to a valid linear SMILES.
